canonical.title: Count subsets with sum equal to k
canonical.sourceFilePath: 05.Recursion/2.Subsequences Pattern/04.Count subsets with sum equal to k.cpp

narrative.title: Assembling Payload Kits that Hit the Target Weight
narrative.scenario: A logistics bench holds crates of known weights and must know how many distinct kit combinations hit an exact payload target. Each crate is either in a kit or out, and the auditor counts kits — not arrangements — so two kits differing only in crate order are the same. Every time the running selection lands exactly on the target, the counter ticks; the answer is reported modulo 10^9 + 7.
narrative.inputFormat: An array arr of n non-negative integers and an integer sum, the target.
narrative.outputFormat: The number of subsets summing to the target, modulo 10^9 + 7.

complexity.optimalTime: O(n * sum) with memoization (the bare source recursion is exponential)

testCases.explanation: Both 1s are distinct crates, so {1a, 4} and {1b, 4} each count.

hintLevels: Level 1: Each crate has a binary choice; a kit is complete when the unspent target hits exactly zero.
Level 2: Recurse over the index with the remaining target: take the crate and subtract, or skip and keep; add the two branch counts.
Level 3: The (index, remaining) pair repeats constantly — memoize it, or this becomes exponential even for small arrays.
